reviewed_invariants: The candidate leaves frozen acceptance/obligations and production compiler/native authentication sources unchanged. Its new required external mail reference is digest-bound as a genuine source input; missing reference refuses preflight before any driver, and changed content invalidates prior provenance.

Actual local HTTPS discovery and JWKS server serve the ephemeral public RSA fixture over a certificate/key created by OpenSSL. The fetch wrapper forwards to native fetch with the fixture CA only for the exact local issuer origin; original request options, signal and real response are preserved. It never substitutes a fetch response or disables TLS verification.

Own exact-byte reconstruction of generated JWT instrumentation proves that its only change is an observation immediately before the native successful return. JOSE signature/issuer/audience/expiry checks and native principal resolution execute. Original/instrumented JWT bytes, actual pinned JOSE tree and ephemeral TLS material digests are captured and validated.

AUTH-003 observes actual RS256 verification, two real provider requests and a native user Alice principal from actual principal-authority SQL. The actual closed TodoPage output validator confirms provider fields are absent. Missing verification, altered provider traffic/key/body, foreign principal/authority and forged clock fail or refuse.

AUTH-004 first performs a real successful Bob JWT request with discovery/JWKS, JOSE verification and native Bob principal authority SQL. Its subsequent Alice-session/Bob-JWT request returns ambiguous_credentials before provider validation, storage access, native principal output or any SQL. Missing or failed positive control and injected ambiguity effects refuse or fail.

AUTH-007 starts with provisioned Alice email and a signed attacker email claim. Actual native JWT resolution and self-service output validation execute; safe before/after user SELECT snapshots remain identical and provider email is absent from output. Changed provisioning, leaked email, missing persistence or foreign output identity fail/refuse.

AUTH-008 has a real signed native api_bearer whose captured lifetime is exactly five minutes. The instrumented native session-storage get entry forwards normally except an explicit unavailable dependency fault. A fresh-authority DELETE positive control accesses get and returns native 503 before authority/business SQL; the same fault remains active while bounded GET succeeds without invoking get or any credential/principal authority query. Its ordinary todo business SELECT remains observable.

The cache fault is injected before native storage access, with actual attempted-read logging and zero credential issuance/principal output on the fault control. No fake authority result is supplied. Missing/inactive controls, unexpected storage access, forged principal, authority SQL or credential issuance are rejected.

Own actual TLS trust counterexamples remove the fixture CA and obtain 503 on both adapters with zero provider handler traffic/verification/principal/SQL. Separate actual different-RSA-key signatures cause two real discovery/JWKS requests then native 401 on both adapters, again with no verified principal or SQL. Generated native verifier bytes remain bound; these negative outputs supply no application pass labels.

All observations exclude actual native credentials, compact JWT strings, CSRF tokens, signing/mail keys and private TLS material. Raw retains public JWK, decoded nonsensitive fixture claims, safe closed identities and public certificate digest only. Ephemeral private TLS file remains in task-owned temporary checkpoint storage; only its digest is retained in integration evidence.

Pre-execution artifact/dependency/TLS bindings are captured before both adapter executions and compared afterward. Own source/reference, original/instrumented JWT, TLS cert/key, actual JOSE dependency, raw certificate trust, extra ledger and missing-compiler challenges refuse, including rebound raw digests with forged issuer trust. Final validation succeeds after restoring every original byte.
